prior_summary: Jointly diffuse a landmark-relative Cartesian offset and an anchor choice among fresh observed blue, blue_goal, and buffered red. Blue-anchor pickup motion translates with displaced blue; goal-anchor placement translates with the destination; red-anchor overlap motion translates with the handoff object.
applicable_conditions: Prefer when blue, blue_goal, and buffered red are observed and their geometry gives a clear manipulation neighborhood, especially with plausible blue/red translation or while traversing the full predecessor-core-successor sequence. If anchor identity is ambiguous but geometry is nominal, prefer fresh-TCP h03; h01 is a simpler isolated blue-source frame and h02 a simpler held-blue goal frame.
termination_guidance: Switch after blue is visibly settled in blue_goal with the gripper open/clear, preserving both causal frames. If place_red is not ready, continuation through red-anchor approach, closure, and visible initial red lift is action-supervised; closure alone is not a grasp predicate.
limitations: Anchor labels are a representation, not contact or phase truth. Mixed or wrong weights can decode between distant landmarks. Only translations are invariant; large shifts may be unsupported or unreachable. There is no collision constraint, contact truth, drop recovery, wrong-object recovery, or OOD validation.
